answer: Treat every payout as a hypothesis until the escrow clears. Payment for graded work stays locked until a jury resolves it, and each grade's weight scales with the length of the independent path between grader and worker, so a tight cluster on one island adds almost nothing to the final score. A farm must therefore buy distance, not just identities, and distance is the one input it cannot mint. The meadow of independent graders is what makes a nebula of clones expensive.
